fields.summary: Behaviour of new constraints in slicing entry
fields.customfield_10618: Add language clarifying that the slice definition entry can apply any constraints that would be allowed if the slice definition element was merely profiling the element.
fields.description:
Since the slicing entry (first "slice" of an element introducing traits of the whole slice) is an ElementDefinition, it can potentially introduce new constraints (even constraints on children of the element).  What is allowed?  We currently say the base definition of the element is repeated here (so open slices can be verified without going back to base) - but what if we have extra constraints?   

         Usecase: It is not unlikely that you want to put a constraint on an element + slice it for other traits.

                     _Note: this is possible using a derived profile, where the slice is re-sliced and not using a <name>, this is supposed to introduce constraints for all slices._

comments.body: I can't think of anything that *shouldn't* be allowed other than something that makes the slicing non-sensical.  (E.g. constraining upper cardinality to 1 or 0 for a repeating slice or constraining to a single type for a type slice or setting a fixed value of either type of slicing).  But all other cardinality, invariant, vocabulary, mustSupport, etc. should be fair game I think.

resolution.description: The proposed change will be made in spirit, but with minor adjustments to reflect committee agreement
resolution.name: Persuasive with Modification
